subject.title: [Feature]: Support Slack Enterprise Grid org installs

question: Should OpenClaw accept the opt-in Slack Enterprise Grid org-install mode proposed in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102372, including workspace-scoped immediate handling and fail-closed detached delivery boundaries?
rationale: The issue is a new Slack account mode and config surface with authorization, session-state, and upgrade implications; repository policy treats those surfaces as maintainer-sensitive even when the source-level gap is clear.

options.title: Review and sponsor the linked PR
options.body: Use the linked pull request as the canonical implementation path and require proof for org-install live behavior plus preserved single-workspace upgrades.

options.title: Keep open for narrower design
options.body: Ask for a smaller design or staged implementation if maintainers want fewer delivery/state surfaces changed in the first pass.

options.title: Decline org-install support for now
options.body: Keep the existing one-account-per-workspace model if maintainers do not want to own Enterprise Grid org-install semantics yet.

recommendation.title: Review and sponsor the linked PR
recommendation.body: Use the linked pull request as the canonical implementation path and require proof for org-install live behavior plus preserved single-workspace upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The current fixed-workspace admission and routing behavior is blamed to this Slack monitor history, making this the best available area-routing owner from source provenance.
